engineVersion: RPG Maker MZ 1.10.00 (Core Scripts v1.10.0, NW.js 0.48.4)

entity_update_cost.description: Simulation update cost per entity across tick cycles
entity_update_cost.implication: Linear entity ticking scales to ~1,000 entities within a 1.8 ms budget (< 11% of a 16.6ms frame). Above 1,000 entities, spatial bucketing or interleaved tick cadences are mandatory.

rendering_cost.description: Depth-sorting overhead (_compareChildOrder) and screen transform cost per visible sprite
rendering_cost.implication: Tilemap depth sorting for up to 5,000 sprites takes < 0.08 ms CPU time. Pixi draw call batching and WebGL fill rate, rather than CPU sorting, constitute the primary rendering bottleneck.

chunk_streaming.description: Cache acquisition, dynamic generation, and eviction behavior across traversal
chunk_streaming.implication: Windowed 3x3 active streaming with 5x5 retention buffer incurs ~0.011 ms per step, confirming that memory remains strictly bounded during continuous traversal.

save_load_performance.description: State serialization and compression benchmarking via JsonEx and pako deflate/inflate
save_load_performance.implication: Pako deflate achieves a 91.1% size reduction (97.4 KB down to 8.6 KB), staying well under RMMZ's 50 KB warning limit. Serialization latency is ~10.6 ms for save and ~7.0 ms for load.

circular_serialization.description: Verification of JsonEx recursion limits and cycle detection absence
circular_serialization.implication: RMMZ JsonEx does not handle circular references; cycles throw an unhandled exception at recursion depth 100. PIXI objects, sprites, functions, and cross-referencing entities must never be passed to save state.

spatial_query_scaling.description: Query latency comparison between global O(N) scan and spatial hash map across increasing object counts
spatial_query_scaling.implication: At 10,000 objects, spatial querying is 15.3x faster than full-world scanning (6.16 us vs 94.24 us). Enforcing spatial indexing is mandatory to maintain 60 FPS under colony workloads.

failure_and_stale_handling.description: Defensive handling of missing chunks and asynchronous request races
failure_and_stale_handling.implication: Boundary clipping and generation tokens safely prevent null dereferences and stale chunk overrides when player transfers rapidly.
